extraction.name: SWE-Gym
extraction.description: SWE-Gym is the first environment for training software engineering (SWE) agents. It contains 2,438 real-world task instances, each comprising a Python codebase with an executable runtime environment, unit tests, and a task specified in natural language. It also includes SWE-Gym Raw (64,689 instances) and SWE-Gym Lite (230 instances).
extraction.creator: Jiayi Pan, Xingyao Wang, Graham Neubig, Navdeep Jaitly, Heng Ji, Alane Suhr, Yizhe Zhang
extraction.citeAs: Pan, J., Wang, X., Neubig, G., Jaitly, N., Ji, H., Suhr, A., & Zhang, Y. (2025). Training Software Engineering Agents and Verifiers with SWE-Gym. arXiv:2412.21139v2.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was constructed by identifying Python repositories using SEART GitHub search, filtering for those created before July 1, 2022, with >500 stars, >300 lines of code, >500 PRs, and >100 contributors. Task instances were extracted from GitHub issues using SWE-Bench's instance extraction script. For a subset of 11 repositories, executable environments were semi-manually configured by setting up dependencies version-by-version using configuration files (e.g., requirements.txt, CI scripts). Instances were validated using SWE-Bench's execution-based validation script to ensure gold patches pass more unit tests than original code.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: GitHub issues and associated code repositories from 358 Python repositories (SWE-Gym Raw) and 11 popular open-source repositories (SWE-Gym).
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Instances were filtered to ensure executable environments could be set up and gold patches passed unit tests. SWE-Gym Lite was delineated by excluding tasks requiring editing more than one file, poorly described problem statements, excessively complex ground-truth code diffs, and tests focused on error message validation.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Executable environments were configured with pre-installed dependencies. Gold patches were validated to ensure they pass more unit tests than the original code. Docker images were pre-built for reproducibility.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotations (labels) were created by validating that the gold patch (human-submitted code diff) passes more unit tests than the original code using SWE-Bench's execution-based validation script. This process required approximately 200 human annotation hours. Annotations were done by a subset of the authors.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Improving automated software engineering capabilities could increase developer productivity and accessibility. However, as agents become more capable, they may impact software engineering jobs. There are considerations around code ownership, licensing, and attribution. Similar techniques could potentially be misused to automate the creation of malicious code.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The task distribution across repositories exhibits a long-tail pattern (e.g., pandas comprises nearly one-third of the total, while bokeh represents one percent). Repeated sampling shows that task success probability follows a long-tail distribution, introducing a bias toward easier tasks.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset is limited by its environment diversity, including the number of repositories, types of tasks, and programming languages. It focuses solely on Python. The current size and repository diversity may not be performance bottlenecks, but further improvements could be achieved with more compute for sampling. Self-improvement results were modest.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training language model-based software engineering agents, training verifier models (reward models) for inference-time scaling, and evaluating agent performance on SWE-Bench Lite and Verified.
